newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour give somes details of windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour give somes details of windfall tax.

text.p: A Labour government might allow Britain's privatised utilities to pay a planned windfall tax in two or more instalments, party officials said on Thursday.
They said a Labour government would spend the money raised over the five-year lifetime of the next parliament on measures to reduce youth and long-term unemployment.

Labour has refused to specify which utilities would be subjected to the tax, or how much might be raised, but one aide noted that equity analysts believe a five billion stg levy has been fully discounted in the stock market.
The aide said Labour was totally confident the planned tax would survive any legal challenge in the courts.
"We're 100 percent sure there are no financial, technical or legal obstacles," he said.
Earlier, deputy Labour leader John Prescott said the levy would be a one-off exercise.

"The levy will be applied to privatised utilities which have gained excess profits. In principle, all privatised utilities will be considered as candidates for the levy without fear or favour," Prescott told parliament.
"There will be no way out through lobbying or through avoidance schemes," Prescott said.
He said Labour would ensure the levey is paid out of excess profits, not higher prices to consumers.
"That's what the regulators are there for and have already made that clear to the companies," Prescott said.
